references.text: Earlier in the same chapter, various unclean creeping things are described, and contact with their dead bodies makes a person unclean.
The preceding verse deals with seed that becomes unclean when a dead creeping thing falls on it, but remains clean if it is dry.
The following verses continue the theme of uncleanness caused by dead animals and how this affects people.
Water plays a role in transmitting uncleanness to objects, just as water on seed makes it susceptible to uncleanness.
Describes how uncleanness from a dead body can be transferred to open vessels and objects, following the principle that moisture makes something susceptible to uncleanness.
Deals with carrion and clean and unclean animals, which is related to the laws concerning uncleanness through contact with dead animals.
